description: The default Windows shortcuts an operator or script author needs most, grouped by task, with what each does and the modifiers that change it. macOS: Cmd for Ctrl, Option for Alt, Ctrl-click for right-click. All are customisable in Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K).

tools.name: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Alt+Z (Undo, Redo, Toggle Last State)
tools.description: Since Photoshop 20.0 (2018) Ctrl+Z steps backward through history repeatedly, Ctrl+Shift+Z steps forward and Ctrl+Alt+Z toggles the last state on and off (the pre-2018 behaviour of Ctrl+Z). The number of steps is limited by Preferences > Performance > History States.
tools.example: Press Ctrl+Z five times to walk back five brush strokes; Ctrl+Alt+Z twice to compare before/after of the last one.
tools.notes: Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts > 'Use Legacy Undo Shortcuts' restores Ctrl+Z as toggle and Ctrl+Alt+Z as step backward. Inside a modal dialog (Levels, Liquify) Ctrl+Z undoes the last change within that dialog.

tools.name: Ctrl+T (Free Transform) and its modifiers
tools.description: Enters Free Transform on the selected layer(s) or selection. While active: drag corner = scale (proportional by default since 20.0; Shift toggles), Alt = from centre, Ctrl-drag corner = distort, Ctrl+Shift-drag side = skew, Ctrl+Alt+Shift-drag corner = perspective, drag outside = rotate (Shift snaps 15 degrees), right-click = mode menu (Warp, Flip...), Enter commits, Esc cancels.
tools.usage: Ctrl+T  |  Ctrl+Shift+T repeats the last transform  |  Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T repeats on a duplicate ('step and repeat')
tools.example: Ctrl+T, type 45 in the rotation field, Enter; then Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T seven times to make a radial pattern of eight copies.
tools.notes: Ctrl+T on a type layer scales the type size; on a Smart Object the transform stays non-destructive. Preferences > Tools > Use Legacy Free Transform reverses the Shift behaviour.

tools.name: Ctrl+J / Ctrl+Shift+J (Layer via Copy / Layer via Cut)
tools.description: Ctrl+J duplicates the selected layer (or copies the current selection to a new layer); Ctrl+Shift+J cuts the selection to a new layer. With multiple layers selected Ctrl+J duplicates them all, preserving order and links.
tools.example: Select Subject, then Ctrl+J to lift the subject onto its own layer for separate grading.
tools.notes: Alt+Ctrl+J opens the Duplicate Layer dialog (name, destination document) in some keyboard sets; otherwise use Layer > Duplicate Layer.

tools.name: Ctrl+Shift+N / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N (New Layer)
tools.description: Ctrl+Shift+N opens the New Layer dialog (name, colour, blend mode, opacity, 'fill with neutral colour'); Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N adds a new empty layer immediately above the current one with no dialog. Alt-click the New Layer button does the same as the dialog; Ctrl-click adds the layer below the current one.
tools.example: Ctrl+Shift+N, Mode Overlay, tick 'Fill with Overlay-neutral color (50% gray)' for a dodge-and-burn layer.
tools.notes: New layers inherit the position above the selected layer and go inside the selected group.

tools.name: Ctrl+E / Ctrl+Shift+E / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E (Merge Down, Merge Visible, Stamp Visible)
tools.description: Ctrl+E merges the selected layer into the one below (or merges all selected layers); Ctrl+Shift+E merges every visible layer; Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E creates a new layer containing a flattened copy of all visible layers while leaving the originals intact (Stamp Visible), the standard way to sharpen or filter a composite non-destructively.
tools.example: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E, then Filter > Camera Raw Filter on the stamped layer while the adjustment stack below stays editable.
tools.notes: Stamp Visible respects layer visibility, not selection. Ctrl+E on a clipping-masked layer merges it with its base.

tools.name: Ctrl+G / Ctrl+Shift+G / Ctrl+Alt+G (Group, Ungroup, Clipping Mask)
tools.description: Ctrl+G puts the selected layers into a new group; Ctrl+Shift+G dissolves the selected group; Ctrl+Alt+G toggles the selected layer as a clipping mask of the layer below (same as Alt-clicking the line between two layers).
tools.example: Add a Curves layer above a subject layer, press Ctrl+Alt+G so the curve affects only the subject.
tools.notes: Ctrl+Alt+G on an adjustment layer is the same as the 'clip to layer' button in the Properties panel.

tools.name: Ctrl+A / Ctrl+D / Ctrl+Shift+D / Ctrl+Shift+I (selection basics)
tools.description: Select All, Deselect, Reselect (restore the last selection) and Inverse. Ctrl+Shift+I after Select Subject is the common way to select the background instead.
tools.example: Select > Subject, Ctrl+Shift+I, then Shift+F5 to Content-Aware Fill the background.
tools.notes: Ctrl+Alt+A selects all layers (not pixels). Ctrl+H hides the marching ants without deselecting (Extras).

tools.name: Ctrl+click layer thumbnail (load transparency as selection) and modifiers
tools.description: Ctrl-clicking a layer, mask or channel thumbnail loads its opaque pixels (or mask/channel luminosity) as a selection. Add Shift to add to the current selection, Alt to subtract, Alt+Shift to intersect. The same modifiers work with Select > Load Selection and with the selection tools.
tools.example: Ctrl-click the RGB channel thumbnail to load the luminosity as a selection, then add a Curves layer: the mask limits it to highlights.
tools.notes: Ctrl-click the RGB composite is the classic luminosity mask; Ctrl+Alt+2 is its shortcut. Ctrl-clicking a type or shape layer loads its outline.

tools.name: Ctrl+L / Ctrl+M / Ctrl+U / Ctrl+B (Levels, Curves, Hue/Saturation, Color Balance dialogs)
tools.description: Open the destructive Image > Adjustments dialogs for the current layer. Adding Alt (e.g. Ctrl+Alt+L) reopens the dialog with the last-used settings. For non-destructive editing use the Adjustments panel instead; these shortcuts are fastest inside actions and on masks/channels.
tools.usage: Ctrl+L  |  Ctrl+M  |  Ctrl+U  |  Ctrl+B  |  add Alt to reuse last settings
tools.example: Alt-click a layer mask to view it, Ctrl+L and drag the black/white points to harden the mask.
tools.notes: Ctrl+Shift+L = Auto Tone, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+L = Auto Contrast, Ctrl+Shift+B = Auto Color.

tools.name: Ctrl+I / Ctrl+Shift+U / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+B (Invert, Desaturate, Black & White)
tools.description: Ctrl+I inverts the layer or mask (essential for flipping a mask from reveal-all to hide-all), Ctrl+Shift+U removes colour in place and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+B opens the Black & White dialog with per-colour luminance sliders.
tools.example: Add a mask, Ctrl+I to hide everything, then paint white to reveal.
tools.notes: On a selection Ctrl+Shift+I inverts the selection, not the pixels.

tools.name: Ctrl+Alt+I / Ctrl+Alt+C (Image Size / Canvas Size)
tools.description: Open the Image Size dialog (resample, dimensions, resolution, method) and the Canvas Size dialog (add/remove canvas around the image with an anchor). Both are also the usual first recorded steps of export actions.
tools.example: Ctrl+Alt+C, tick Relative, add 100 px width and height, anchor centre, extension colour white - a quick border.
tools.notes: Image Rotation, Trim and Reveal All have no default shortcuts; assign them in Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts if used often.

tools.name: Ctrl+R / Ctrl+; / Ctrl+' / Ctrl+H (Rulers, Guides, Grid, Extras)
tools.description: Toggle rulers, guides, the document grid and all Extras (selection edges, layer edges, smart guides, target paths, slices, count, notes) at once. Ctrl+Alt+; locks guides; Ctrl+Shift+H toggles the target path only; Ctrl+Shift+; toggles Snap.
tools.usage: Ctrl+R  |  Ctrl+;  |  Ctrl+'  |  Ctrl+H  |  Ctrl+Alt+;  |  Ctrl+Shift+;
tools.example: Ctrl+H hides the marching ants to judge an edge while keeping the selection active.
tools.notes: On first use Ctrl+H on macOS asks whether it should hide Photoshop or Extras. Drag from a ruler to create a guide; Alt-drag switches orientation.

tools.name: Ctrl+0 / Ctrl+1 / Ctrl++ / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+Alt+0 (zoom levels)
tools.description: Fit on Screen, 100 % (actual pixels), zoom in, zoom out and 100 % again through the legacy Ctrl+Alt+0. Double-clicking the Hand tool is another Fit on Screen, double-clicking the Zoom tool another 100 %. View > 200 % and View > Fit Layer(s) on Screen have no default shortcuts.
tools.example: Ctrl+1 before judging sharpening, Ctrl+0 to see the whole composition.
tools.notes: Alt+scroll wheel zooms around the pointer; Shift+scroll scrolls horizontally. Preferences > Tools > Zoom with Scroll Wheel makes plain scrolling zoom.

tools.name: Space / Ctrl+Space / Alt+Space / R (temporary Hand, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Rotate View)
tools.description: Holding Space turns any tool into the Hand tool for panning (Space-drag, or Space-click with flick panning); Ctrl+Space-drag zooms in scrubby style (drag right = in), Alt+Space zooms out; holding R gives the Rotate View tool (drag to rotate the canvas, Esc resets, Shift snaps to 15 degrees). Releasing the key returns to the previous tool.
tools.example: While painting, hold R and drag to tilt the canvas 30 degrees for a comfortable stroke angle, then release; press Esc later to reset rotation.
tools.notes: Spring-loaded tools: holding any tool letter temporarily switches to it and releasing returns. Space also works while a modal transform is active.

tools.name: Tab / Shift+Tab / F (hide panels, screen modes)
tools.description: Tab hides or shows all panels, the toolbar and the options bar; Shift+Tab hides only the panels; F cycles Standard Screen, Full Screen with Menu Bar and Full Screen (black background, no UI; Esc returns). Together they give a distraction-free view for presenting or painting.
tools.example: Press F twice and Tab for a full-screen black presentation of the image; press F again (or Esc) to return.
tools.notes: With panels hidden, Preferences > Workspace > Auto-Show Hidden Panels reveals them when the pointer touches the screen edge.

tools.name: D / X (default colours, swap colours)
tools.description: D resets the foreground/background swatches to black/white (when a mask or channel is targeted the defaults become white foreground/black background, i.e. reversed), and X swaps them. Painting on masks is done almost entirely with these two keys.
tools.example: Click a layer mask, press D then paint (white reveals); press X and paint to hide.
tools.notes: Alt+Backspace fills with the foreground colour, Ctrl+Backspace with the background colour.

tools.name: [ and ] / Shift+[ and Shift+] (brush size and hardness)
tools.description: Decrease/increase the brush tip size for any brush-based tool (steps scale with size), and decrease/increase hardness in 25 % steps. Alt+right-drag (Windows) horizontally resizes and vertically changes hardness with an on-canvas HUD preview.
tools.example: Hold Alt and right-drag left to shrink the brush while watching the red preview circle.
tools.notes: Preferences > Tools > 'Vary Round Brush Hardness based on HUD vertical movement' enables the vertical hardness drag. Bracket keys are also used by Ctrl+[ ] for layer order.

tools.name: Number keys 0-9 (opacity / fill / flow)
tools.description: With a painting tool active, single digits set the tool Opacity (1 = 10 %, 5 = 50 %, 0 = 100 %; two digits typed quickly give exact values like 35) and Shift+digit sets Flow. With a non-painting tool (Move, selection) the same keys set the layer Opacity and Shift+digit sets layer Fill. 00 gives 0 %.
tools.example: With the Move tool active press 5 to set the layer to 50 % opacity; Shift+5 sets Fill 50 % (affecting only pixels, not effects).
tools.notes: If Airbrush mode is on, the digits set Flow and Shift+digit sets Opacity (swapped).

tools.name: Shift++ / Shift+- and Shift+Alt+letter (blend modes)
tools.description: Shift+plus and Shift+minus cycle the blend mode of the active layer (or the painting tool's mode when a brush tool is selected) forward/backward through the list; Shift+Alt+letter jumps directly (N Normal, I Dissolve, M Multiply, S Screen, O Overlay, F Soft Light, H Hard Light, E Difference, C Color, Y Luminosity, and so on - see the per-mode entries).
tools.example: Select a texture layer with the Move tool and press Shift++ repeatedly to audition every blend mode.
tools.notes: With a painting tool active the shortcuts change the tool blend mode instead; switch to the Move tool (V) first for layers.

tools.name: Q (Quick Mask toggle)
tools.description: Toggles Quick Mask mode, turning the selection into a paintable red overlay and back. Painting black masks (deselects), white selects; any filter can be applied to the mask while in this mode.
tools.example: Q, Gradient tool black-to-white drag, Q - a graduated selection for a sky adjustment.
tools.notes: Double-click the Quick Mask button to change the overlay colour/meaning. Scripting: `doc.quickMaskMode`.

tools.name: Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S / Ctrl+Alt+S / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+W (Save, Save As, Save a Copy, Save for Web, Export As)
tools.description: Save in place, Save As (new name/format, becomes the working file), Save a Copy (introduced 22.4 - writes a copy in any format without changing the open document), Save for Web (Legacy) and Export As. Save As for layered documents only offers formats that keep layers unless legacy Save As is enabled in preferences.
tools.example: Ctrl+S to save the PSD, then Ctrl+Alt+S to write a JPEG copy for the client without leaving the PSD.
tools.notes: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S was Save for Web since CS2; Export As has no shortcut before CC 2015 keyboard sets. Cloud documents use the same shortcuts and save to Creative Cloud.

tools.name: Ctrl+N / Ctrl+O / Ctrl+Alt+O / Ctrl+W / Ctrl+Alt+W / Ctrl+Shift+W / Ctrl+Q (document management)
tools.description: New document dialog, Open, Browse in Bridge, Close, Close All, Close and Go to Bridge, Quit. Ctrl+Alt+Shift+O is Open As (choose the format module explicitly). Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycle between open document tabs.
tools.usage: Ctrl+N  |  Ctrl+O  |  Ctrl+Alt+O  |  Ctrl+W  |  Ctrl+Alt+W  |  Ctrl+Shift+W  |  Ctrl+Q  |  Ctrl+Tab
tools.example: Copy an image to the clipboard, Ctrl+N (the preset defaults to clipboard size), Enter, Ctrl+V.
tools.notes: Ctrl+Alt+W closing all documents prompts once per unsaved document; scripts should use `doc.close(SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES)` instead.

tools.name: Ctrl+K / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+M / Ctrl+Shift+K (Preferences, Keyboard Shortcuts, Menus, Color Settings)
tools.description: Open the Preferences dialog (General pane), the Keyboard Shortcuts editor (Application Menus, Panel Menus, Tools, Taskspaces sets), the Menus editor (hide or colour menu items and save sets) and Color Settings.
tools.example: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K > Application Menus > File > Scripts > MyExport.jsx, assign F12, Save Set.
tools.notes: Shortcut conflicts are flagged in the dialog; 'Summarize' exports an HTML list of the set.

tools.name: Ctrl+Alt+R / Ctrl+Shift+X / Ctrl+Alt+V / Ctrl+Shift+A / Ctrl+Shift+R (Select and Mask, Liquify, Vanishing Point, Camera Raw Filter, Lens Correction)
tools.description: Open the five modal workspaces/filters directly. Select and Mask needs a selection tool or mask context; Camera Raw Filter and Liquify work best on Smart Objects so they stay editable. Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A opens Adaptive Wide Angle.
tools.usage: Ctrl+Alt+R  |  Ctrl+Shift+X  |  Ctrl+Alt+V  |  Ctrl+Shift+A  |  Ctrl+Shift+R  |  Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A
tools.example: Convert to Smart Object, Ctrl+Shift+A for Camera Raw Filter, tweak, then Ctrl+Shift+X to Liquify - both re-editable from the Layers panel.
tools.notes: Before CC 2015.5 Refine Edge used Ctrl+Alt+R; the shortcut carried over to Select and Mask. Content-Aware Fill (workspace) and Sky Replacement have no default shortcuts.

tools.name: Ctrl+Alt+F / Ctrl+Shift+F (Last Filter, Fade)
tools.description: Ctrl+Alt+F re-applies the last filter with the same settings; Ctrl+Shift+F opens Edit > Fade to reduce the opacity or change the blend mode of the last filter, adjustment or brush stroke - it must be used immediately after the operation.
tools.example: Filter > Sharpen > Unsharp Mask, then Ctrl+Shift+F, Mode Luminosity, Opacity 70 %.
tools.notes: Ctrl+F is Search (Discover panel) since 20.0. Fade is unavailable once any other command has run.

tools.name: Alt+Backspace / Ctrl+Backspace / Shift+Backspace / Shift+F5 (fill shortcuts)
tools.description: Fill the selection (or layer) with the foreground colour, the background colour, or open the Fill dialog (Content-Aware, Pattern, History, 50 % gray...). Adding Shift (Alt+Shift+Backspace, Ctrl+Shift+Backspace) fills only the opaque pixels, preserving transparency. Backspace/Delete on a Background layer fills with the background colour; on a normal layer it clears to transparent.
tools.usage: Alt+Backspace  |  Ctrl+Backspace  |  Shift+Backspace or Shift+F5  |  Alt+Shift+Backspace / Ctrl+Shift+Backspace (preserve transparency)
tools.example: Select a text layer's transparency (Ctrl-click), new layer, Alt+Backspace to fill the text shape with the foreground colour.
tools.notes: Ctrl+Backspace on a layer mask fills it with the background colour (white by default in mask context).

tools.name: Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Y (Proof Colors, Gamut Warning)
tools.description: Toggle soft-proofing against the profile chosen in View > Proof Setup, and the out-of-gamut overlay for that profile. Both are essential before converting to CMYK or sending to a print lab.
tools.example: View > Proof Setup > Working CMYK, then Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Y while pulling saturation with a Hue/Saturation layer.
tools.notes: In some keyboard sets Ctrl+Y is Redo (legacy Photoshop 6 behaviour); check Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts.

tools.name: F5 / F6 / F7 / F8 / Alt+F9 (Brush Settings, Color, Layers, Info, Actions panels)
tools.description: Toggle the most-used panels: F5 Brush Settings, F6 Color, F7 Layers, F8 Info, Alt+F9 Actions (F9 alone on macOS). Useful with panels hidden (Tab) to bring one up temporarily.
tools.example: Tab to hide everything, F7 when you need the Layers panel, F7 again to hide it.
tools.notes: Other panels have no default shortcut; assign them in Keyboard Shortcuts > Application Menus > Window.

tools.name: Ctrl+[ / Ctrl+] / Ctrl+Shift+[ / Ctrl+Shift+] (layer stacking order)
tools.description: Send the selected layer(s) backward / bring forward by one position, or send to back / bring to front within the current group. Works with multiple selected layers and keeps their relative order.
tools.example: Select the new 'shadow' layer and press Ctrl+[ to move it beneath the subject.
tools.notes: A layer cannot be moved below the Background layer; unlock it first.

tools.name: Alt+[ / Alt+] / Alt+, / Alt+. (select next/previous/bottom/top layer)
tools.description: Change the active layer from the keyboard: Alt+[ selects the layer below, Alt+] the layer above, Alt+, the bottom layer and Alt+. the top layer. Adding Shift (Alt+Shift+[ / ]) extends the selection to include the neighbouring layer; Alt+Shift+, / . select from the current layer to the bottom/top.
tools.usage: Alt+[  |  Alt+]  |  Alt+,  |  Alt+.  |  add Shift to extend
tools.example: Alt+. then Alt+Shift+, selects every layer, ready for Ctrl+G.
tools.notes: Hidden layers are included in the traversal. Ctrl+Alt+A selects all layers directly.

tools.name: Ctrl+C / Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+V / Ctrl+Shift+V / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V (Copy, Copy Merged, Paste, Paste in Place, Paste Into)
tools.description: Copy the selection from the active layer; Copy Merged copies the composite of all visible layers in the selection; Paste creates a new layer centred in view; Paste in Place keeps the original coordinates; Paste Into pastes inside the current selection and creates a layer mask from it (Paste Outside is in the Edit > Paste Special menu without a default shortcut).
tools.example: Select a window, Ctrl+Shift+C on the composite, switch documents, Ctrl+Shift+V to place it at the same coordinates.
tools.notes: Pasting between documents of different colour profiles triggers the Paste Profile Mismatch dialog unless disabled in Color Settings.

tools.name: Enter / Ctrl+Enter / Esc (commit and cancel)
tools.description: Enter commits a transform, crop or dialog; Ctrl+Enter commits text editing (Enter inserts a line break there) and also converts a path to a selection when a path is targeted; Esc cancels a transform, crop, text edit or dialog. In the Layers panel Enter also opens a layer's name for editing.
tools.example: Draw a path with the Pen tool, Ctrl+Enter to load it as a selection, Ctrl+J to lift it to a layer.
tools.notes: Numeric keypad Enter also commits text. Ctrl+. (period) cancels a running action.

tools.name: Alt+click mask / Shift+click mask / \ (view, disable, overlay layer mask)
tools.description: Alt-click a layer-mask thumbnail to view the mask as a greyscale image on the canvas (again to return); Shift-click disables the mask (red X); Alt+Shift-click shows it as a rubylith overlay; the backslash key toggles that overlay too. Ctrl-click loads it as a selection. Right-click the mask for Mask Options and Select and Mask.
tools.usage: Alt+click mask thumbnail  |  Shift+click  |  Alt+Shift+click or \  |  Ctrl+click
tools.example: Alt-click the mask, Ctrl+L to increase contrast in the mask, Alt-click to return to the composite.
tools.notes: The same clicks work on vector masks (Shift to disable) and Smart Filter masks. Properties panel > Density/Feather edit masks non-destructively.

tools.name: Alt+drag (Move tool duplicate) and Ctrl+Alt+drag
tools.description: With the Move tool, Alt-drag duplicates the selected layer(s) or selection contents to the drop position; with any other tool Ctrl+Alt-drag does the same (Ctrl temporarily selects the Move tool). Shift constrains the drag to 45 degree angles; arrow keys nudge 1 px (Shift+arrow 10 px), and Alt+arrow nudges a duplicate.
tools.usage: V (Move tool) + Alt+drag  |  Ctrl+Alt+drag (any tool)  |  Arrow / Shift+Arrow  |  Alt+Arrow
tools.example: With the Move tool, Shift+Alt-drag a button layer straight down to drop a duplicate directly beneath it; press Alt+Down a few times to nudge another copy into place.
tools.notes: Alt-drag in the Layers panel also duplicates a layer to the drop position; Alt-drag a mask thumbnail copies the mask to another layer.

tools.name: Tool letter shortcuts (V M L W C K I J B S Y E G O P T A U H R Z) and Shift-cycling
tools.description: Every toolbar slot has a letter: V Move/Artboard, M Marquee, L Lasso (incl. Selection Brush), W Object Selection/Quick Selection/Magic Wand, C Crop/Perspective Crop/Slice, K Frame, I Eyedropper/Color Sampler/Ruler/Note/Count, J Healing/Spot Healing/Remove/Patch/Content-Aware Move/Red Eye, B Brush/Pencil/Color Replacement/Mixer/Adjustment Brush, S Clone/Pattern Stamp, Y History/Art History Brush, E Erasers, G Gradient/Paint Bucket, O Dodge/Burn/Sponge, P Pen tools, T Type tools, A Path/Direct Selection, U Shape tools, H Hand, R Rotate View, Z Zoom. Shift+letter cycles the tools sharing a slot; holding the letter spring-loads the tool temporarily.
tools.example: Press L, then Shift+L until the Selection Brush is active; hold B briefly to paint one stroke and release to return.
tools.notes: Blur/Sharpen/Smudge have no letter by default. Preferences > Tools > Use Shift Key for Tool Switch off makes the bare letter cycle. Customise under Keyboard Shortcuts > Tools.

tools.name: Caps Lock (precise cursor toggle)
tools.description: Switches painting-tool cursors between the brush-tip outline and the precise crosshair while held on. A frequent support question ('my brush cursor turned into a crosshair') is simply Caps Lock being on.
tools.example: Turn Caps Lock on for pixel-accurate clicks with the Clone Stamp source, off to see the brush size again.
tools.notes: Preferences > Cursors sets the default cursor types that Caps Lock toggles between.

tools.name: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+I / Ctrl+P / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P (File Info, Print, Print One Copy)
tools.description: Open the File Info (XMP metadata) dialog, the Print dialog with colour management and layout, and print one copy immediately with the last settings.
tools.example: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+I to add copyright and description before export; the same fields feed Content Credentials producer info.
tools.notes: File Info templates (.xmp) can be exported from the dialog's menu.

tools.name: Ctrl+F (Search / Discover) and F1 (Help)
tools.description: Since Photoshop 20.0 Ctrl+F opens the in-app Search (now the Discover panel) to find and run menu commands, tools, panels, tutorials and Stock assets by name; F1 opens the online Help. Search is the fastest way to run a buried command without memorising its location.
tools.example: Ctrl+F, type 'content-aware scale', Enter - the command runs.
tools.notes: Ctrl+F was 'Last Filter' before 20.0; that moved to Ctrl+Alt+F.

tools.name: Ctrl+Alt+2 / Ctrl+2 / Ctrl+3-6 (composite and channel targeting)
tools.description: Ctrl+2 targets the composite (RGB/CMYK) channel and Ctrl+3, 4, 5 (and 6 for CMYK) target the individual colour channels for editing; Ctrl+Alt+2 loads the composite luminosity as a selection (Ctrl+Alt+3-6 load single channels). Ctrl+\ targets the layer mask; Ctrl+2 returns to the image.
tools.example: Ctrl+Alt+2 for a luminosity selection, Ctrl+Shift+I to invert it to shadows, then add a Curves layer.
tools.notes: Ctrl+~ was the composite shortcut in versions before CS4.
